newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: IFRC says 13 Afghan refugees die in Turkmenistan.
newsitem.headline: IFRC says 13 Afghan refugees die in Turkmenistan.

text.p: A Red Cross official said on Thursday that 13 people among some 8,000 Afghan refugees who fled to Turkmenistan last week from their war-ravaged homeland had died, mostly from poor sanitation.

"All in all, 13 refugees have died since last week," Thorir Gudmundsson, regional information delegate for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.

Referring to reports obtained by satellite phone from the federation's workers aiding the refugees in Turkmenistan, Gudmundsson said that most of those who had died were children suffering from diarrhoea.
The three refugee camps are in a no-man's land in the desert on the Turkmen side of the Turkmen-Afghan border.
"This place is very inhospitable...Today it was even 'cool', and temperatures did not rise above 45 centigrade (113 Fahrenheit)," Gudmundsson said.
He added there was a hope that despite poor sanitary conditions a major outbreak of infectious deseases would be avoided.
"The refugees are currently undergoing vaccination by another group of aid workers -- Medicins Sans Frontieres -- who are also in the area," he said.

The refugees fled from the town of Mari Chak on the Afghan side of the Murgab river, which separates the two states, to escape fighting in northern Afghanistan where forces of the purist Taleban militia have clashed with troops of Uzbek General Abdul Malik.
The Taleban are trying to regain control of territories in the north they briefly won and then lost to the anti-Taleban alliance in May.
Having fled the fighting the refugees now face another enemy -- a shortage of food.

Gudmundsson said a convoy of several trucks with food and medicines sent by the federation's branch in Tajikistan on Wednesday was on its way to the refugee camps near the Turkmen town of Takhta Bazar.

"Local Turkmen authorities have also agreed to make available some seven tonnes of food, including wheat flour, rice and salt, which will be enough for one or two days before the convoy arrives," he said.
Turkmenistan's rural regions are themselves short of food.

"This is a very considerable gesture in view of the food situation in this area of Turkmenistan," said Gudmundsson, quoting a Red Cross worker in the area commenting on the action by local authorities.
The refugees at Takhta Bazar are the first major influx of displaced Afghans to one of the ex-Soviet Central Asian states.
Former Soviet republics neighbouring Afghanistan have voiced fears that fighting there could trigger an exodus of civilians.
